advice: Experiment: in the n=512 Strassen path, replace the three dense 256×256 workspaces with one 768 KiB allocation, then divide it into left, right, and product buffers. Keep the seven products, FP32 arithmetic, accumulation order, and recombination unchanged. Fully write both operands before each helper call; the beta-zero helper overwrites the full product buffer, so no workspace clearing is needed. Free the block before gemm returns. If allocation fails, use the correct existing fallback. This differs from the measured three-allocation Strassen source. Hypothesis: one allocation and free may reduce allocator overhead; benefit is unknown.
risks: The measured three-buffer Strassen wrapper lost all ten paired comparisons against its controls, but those joint results do not identify allocation as the cause. This change retains its arithmetic and packing work, so it may not improve total time. One 768 KiB allocation may fail where three smaller allocations would succeed. Before timing, check fresh inputs, input preservation, full output overwrite and guards, tolerance 0.002 including cancellation and scale-separated cases, allocation-failure fallback, general sizes, tails, and n<=0. If correct, collect ten candidate validations and ten alternating paired controls under unchanged settings, then apply the fixed promotion and held-out gates. No speedup is established.
